domain_title: Constitutional Transparency and the People's Ledger
research_domain_title: Constitutional Transparency, Public Records, and Accountability Systems
note: Fourth institutional spine. Architecture and developing doctrine only — not a finished open-records statute. Presumption of openness with legitimate exceptions. No invented FOIA statistics or portal coverage claims.
role_in_philosophy: Constitutional transparency is not the claim that everything government does is public. It is a presumption of openness with constitutionally and legally justified exceptions, so power remains reviewable while privacy, safety, and national security remain protected.

guiding_principle.text: In a constitutional republic, government does not own public information. It holds public information in trust for the people, subject only to those limited protections necessary to preserve constitutional rights, legitimate privacy, public safety, and national security.

openness_presumption.text: Government information created with public resources should be presumed open unless there is a constitutionally or legally justified reason to protect it. The burden should generally be on the government to explain why information is withheld.

legitimate_exceptions_examples: other information whose disclosure could violate privacy or create serious safety risks
exceptions_rule: Exceptions must be grounded in law, narrowly tailored, explained, and subject to review. Secrecy is not the default.

digital_trail_doctrine.summary: Every government action should leave a digital trail so the public can see what happened, who authorized it, why it happened, how much it cost, what outcome was expected, and whether it succeeded.

peoples_ledger.name: The People's Ledger
peoples_ledger.definition: Not a financial ledger alone — a constitutional accountability ledger: a searchable portal where every public dollar and major public action has a traceable story.
peoples_ledger.note: Named instrument and architecture — not an operating statewide portal. Do not invent coverage statistics.

public_dashboard.summary: Every agency should publish a living accountability page — not a press-release page — that ordinary citizens can understand.
public_dashboard.rule: Citizens should not need specialized knowledge to understand how an agency is performing.

traceable_law.summary: Every statute should be selectable with its full public history, not only the final text.

public_procurement.summary: Every contract should be searchable, subject to legitimate confidentiality protections where required by law.

open_budgets.rule: The public should be able to follow a dollar from appropriation to expenditure.

ai_for_transparency.rule: AI should help citizens understand government — not replace government or become the official record.
example_queries: Show me every transportation project in my county over the last five years.
Which agencies spent the most on outside consultants?
How many contracts were completed on time?

public_access_equity.summary: Transparency must not depend on whether someone owns a computer or has reliable internet.

identity_and_access_balance.caution: Requiring identity disclosure for routine viewing of ordinary public records can chill journalists, whistleblowers, business owners, activists, and curious citizens.
identity_and_access_balance.routine_public_records: Freely accessible without unnecessary barriers, while protecting systems against abuse through reasonable cybersecurity measures.
identity_and_access_balance.sensitive_or_high_volume: Authentication, rate limits, or licensing where needed to protect security, privacy, or system integrity.

constitutional_transparency_test.title: Constitutional Transparency Test
constitutional_transparency_test.purpose: Screen transparency, records, procurement, and accountability reforms before acceptance into the framework.

questions.text: Is this funded with public money?
Can the public understand its purpose?
Can the public measure its success?
Can the public review how money was spent?
Is any information withheld? If so, why?
Is the reason for withholding grounded in law and subject to review?
Is there an independent audit trail?
Can future generations understand what happened and why?

research_status.next: Phase 2.1: register FOIA/open-records statutes, state transparency portals, procurement publication standards, and budget-transparency evaluations without inventing coverage rates
